subject: Priority decision request: dedicated GPU tranche assignment for ApexData
messages:
From: Tom Reynolds <tom@apexdata.ai>
To: alex_martinez@redwood.ai
Cc: ApexData Legal <legal@apexdata.ai>
Date: Wed, 07 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated capacity ask — urgency and contract implications

Alex,

Thanks for the demo last week. We’ve run the pilot against the 13B model and are seeing production-ish latency at peak that will require dedicated GPU capacity to meet our SLA commitments to enterprise customers. Legal is ready to sign but needs a clear commitment on the tranche allocation and whether preemption is allowed during our launch window (May 1–Jun 30).

We were quoted a 12-GPU tranche with hot-path reservation; can you confirm whether that’s deduped from other reserved contracts or if it’s on-net (no preemption)? If preemption is possible, we need guardrails in the contract (max preempt hours/month, notice window, and automatic fallbacks to a compatible quantized variant).

Attaching our SOC/security checklist and a simple throughput runbook.

Tom
VP Product, ApexData

Attachments referenced: ApexData_MATP_v03.pdf, throughput-log-20270328.txt
From: alex_martinez@redwood.ai
To: Tom Reynolds <tom@apexdata.ai>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 07 Apr 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity ask — urgency and contract implications

Tom — thanks for the detail and the attachments. Quick answers up front: the 12-GPU tranche you were quoted was modeled as a Dedicated Reservation (no preemption) in the original sizing exercise; the only time we would reclaim capacity is under a formal overflow/failure scenario after attempted regional fallbacks. That said, we need an executive sign-off for the hot-path guarantees because we’re currently balancing two other near-term commitments (see below).

Ben, Marissa, Laura — looping you in because this is now an Allocation decision. ApexData is asking to lock a 12xA100-equivalent tranche with hot-path reservation for 60 days starting May 1. Competing requests: 1) HelioHealth (reserved Q2 scale-up, mid-tier SLA) and 2) Nimbus Labs (recently closed ARR, small burst). We have limited headroom in the us-west hot pool during May.

Ask: can we confirm prioritization (ApexData vs HelioHealth vs Nimbus) and whether we authorize preemption protections for ApexData in the SOW? If we can’t commit to no-preempt, we should bake in the quantized model fallback and a 4-hour notice clause.

I’ve attached a proposed tranche mapping for your review.

—Alex
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: ben_carter@redwood.ai
To: alex_martinez@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 08 Apr 2027 08:21:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity ask — urgency and contract implications

Quick summary from capacity planning intake: we have approx 28 A100-equivalent GPUs free in the us-west pool for May after current rollouts are applied. Commitments in flight: HelioHealth plans to add 8 GPUs (committed) and Nimbus has an uplift ask for 6 GPUs but is willing to take preemptible excess. ApexData’s 12 would consume the majority of the remaining headroom and would block our flexibility for emergency failover.

Recommendation (ops + sales tradeoff):
- Approve ApexData 12 GPUs as a Dedicated Reservation only if ApexData signs a 9-month committed term or pays a one-time hot-path premium (20% uplift) to compensate for blocking headroom.
- Otherwise offer 8 Dedicated + 4 preemptible burst with contractual fallback to a quantized 8-bit variant for the preemptible portion and a 4-hour notification SLA for preemptions.

Marissa — this is a commercial decision (discount/term). Laura — need legal for the preemption notice window. If leadership wants to keep max flexibility for enterprise rollouts in May, we keep the tranche smaller.

Ben
Principal Product Ops, Redwood Inference

Attachment: proposed-tranche-mapping.xlsx
From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: ben_carter@redwood.ai, alex_martinez@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 09 Apr 2027 16:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity ask — urgency and contract implications

Thanks — I agree with Ben’s recommendation. For prioritization, we should treat ApexData as high-priority but only if they either: (a) commit to the longer term, or (b) pay the hot-path premium. We can’t stretch the no-preempt promise without material commercial compensation given the production roadmap congestion in May.

Concrete decision requested by next EOD Monday:
- Option A (preferred): Approve 12x Dedicated, require 9-month term or equivalent prepayment; include hard SLA (max 8 preempt hours over term) and automatic downgrade path to the agreed quantized variant for any forced preemption events.
- Option B (fallback): Approve 8x Dedicated + 4x Preemptible burst with 4-hour notice window and defined fallback model.

Alex — please confirm ApexData’s willingness to sign to either option and confirm whether legal needs the SLA language before they execute. If Apex wavers, we move to Option B and reallocate remaining headroom for HelioHealth.

—Marissa
Director, Strategic Accounts, Redwood Inference
